Codex pre-review (not a collaborator review; no marker) @ fabdbcac6bfa5133a2c9e13f568c9efd32e401e9

Verdict FINDINGS

- P1 — crates/app/src/mcp/align_tools.rs:71: Align a cylinder to X with angle_deg=21, then the same pick to Y with angle_deg=33 and flip=true. Both calls succeed, but the stored transform sends the original Z cylinder axis to [0.8386705679, 0, -0.5446390350], perpendicular to Y. This can machine the wrong face. A temporary extension of the cylinder pin failed on this case. The existing backend at crates/app/src/pick/cylinder.rs:218-220 reads view_pose (including the active alignment), then applies the supplied alignment again. Fix the shared path and pin consecutive alignments before exposing it here.
- .claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md:150: This process-file change lacks the required `Process change: yes` line in the PR body (AGENTS.md process-change rule).

Tests: all three named pins GREEN. Quick gate GREEN: 326 passed, 1 ignored. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` GREEN. Local merge with upstream/main succeeded.

Mutations: target RED; angle RED; source RED; point RED; vertex-with-point RED; box-with-pick RED; unchanged-origin RED; cylinder setup bypass RED; origin setup bypass RED. Finite-filter removal GREEN (JSON numbers cannot carry nonfinite values). Missing-pick guards replaced with Null fallback GREEN for both tools; missing-pick pins are absent and shared pick validation still rejects Null. All mutations restored; final three pins GREEN; worktree clean.

Other checks: changed Rust files are under 400 lines; no new production unwrap/expect/panic; no golden changes or prohibited PNG, PROCESS_VERSION, dependency, .github or scripts changes. Changelog and Fixes lines present. No code pushed and no labels changed.

Fixed both findings at head `88bb7244558e12ca33aeb9f73eb49dbcabf54377`.

`consecutive_cylinder_alignments_land_the_original_axis` pins the consecutive alignment case.

Codex pre-review (not a collaborator review; no marker) @ 88bb7244558e12ca33aeb9f73eb49dbcabf54377

Verdict FINDINGS

- P1 — crates/app/src/mcp/align_tools.rs:100: A vertex origin for an explicitly named setup uses the active setup's alignment, silently storing the wrong WCS origin. Import cylinder(20,10,48) and a cube [30,40,50]..[40,50,60]; align Setup1's cylinder to X; add unaligned Setup2. Placing Setup1's origin at cube vertex `vertex:0x1d6c85d701a52375` returns [30,50,50]. Undo, activate Setup1, and repeat the identical request: [35,35,60]. The helper calls `pick::align::vertex`, which uses `setup_align::view_pose`. Resolve the vertex through the named setup's pose and pin this case. An external MCP harness reproduced the mismatch with a failing equality assertion.

Local trial merge with upstream/main succeeded. All four MCP pins passed. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: 336 passed, one ignored. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

Mutation checks: target, angle parser, source, point, vertex-with-point, box-with-pick, unchanged-origin, flip and restoring the old cylinder axis transform each compiled and made its pin RED. Removing only the finite-number filter stayed GREEN; JSON cannot carry non-finite numbers. All mutations were restored, and the four pins passed again. Replacing missing-setup guards with a Setup1 fallback stayed GREEN in both handlers; no missing-setup case is pinned. Replacing required-pick guards with null fallbacks stayed GREEN in both handlers; downstream pick validation still refuses null. The final restored suite passed all four pins and the worktree is clean.

Rule checks passed: no added production unwrap/expect/panic, changed Rust files under 400 lines, no changed goldens or snapshot PNGs, PROCESS_VERSION, dependencies, .github or scripts. Body includes Changelog:, Fixes #1586 and Process change: yes. No lasting code changes or pushes.

Fixed the named-setup vertex origin finding at head `a964ad4a3803b3472252b1b47fe270c02b3946c7`.

The shared origin command now resolves the vertex through the requested setup's pose.
`named_setup_vertex_origin_uses_its_pose_when_inactive` pins the same result with Setup1 active or inactive, the expected [35,35,60] origin, undo, and Setup2 isolation.
Restoring the old lookup made the pin fail with [30,50,50] versus [35,35,60].
Restoring the fix made it pass.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: 360 passed and one ignored.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

Please re-review the new head.

- All five MCP orientation tests passed, including all three pins named in the body. All five passed again after restoration.
- Quick gate: RED. 359 passed, one failed, one ignored. `crates/app/tests/winding_align.rs:189` expects InsideOut but receives Outward. The same failure reproduced with all four changed production files replaced by upstream/main versions. This is an upstream failure.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- Mutations: target, angle parser, source, point, vertex-with-point, box-with-pick, unchanged origin, flip, cylinder frame, and named vertex frame each produced assertion RED. All edits were restored.
- Removing only the finite-number filter stayed GREEN. JSON numbers cannot represent nonfinite values; the malformed-angle parser mutation was RED.
- Extra safety case passed: inactive Setup1 aligned the original cylinder axis to Z while active Setup2 held a different alignment. Setup2 stayed unchanged; undo and redo restored the expected poses.
- Source files remain below 400 lines. No new production unwrap/expect/panic, changed goldens, snapshot PNGs, PROCESS_VERSION, Cargo dependencies, .github, or scripts. Body contains Changelog: and Fixes #1586.

No code retained, pushed, or labels changed.

Ready for the maintainer to merge. No defects specific to this PR were found. The local quick gate has one upstream test failure, as detailed below.

The two tools use the shared commands and command history. The tests check tool discovery, named refusals, axis placement, setup isolation, and undo. The cylinder frame and named setup vertex fixes address the earlier reports. The body has `Changelog:`, `Process change: yes`, and `Fixes #1586`.

Local results after a clean trial merge with upstream/main `703af818`:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| App test build through the quick gate | Passed |
| App unit tests | 305 passed, 1 ignored |
| centre_pick | 8 passed |
| mcp_align_axes | 2 passed |
| mcp_lay_face | 1 passed |
| mcp_orient_dropdowns | 5 passed |
| mcp_setup | 9 passed |
| orient_dropdowns | 9 passed |
| plane_align | 9 passed |
| wcs_align | 5 passed |
| winding_align | 8 passed, 1 failed |
| `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` failed with 361 passed, 1 failed, and 1 ignored. The failure is at `crates/app/tests/winding_align.rs:189`:

```text
the_inside_out_stl_fixture_reads_inside_out_and_refuses
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: [Outward]
 right: [InsideOut]
```

I replaced all four changed production files with their upstream/main versions and ran this test again. It failed with the same result. This failure is present without this PR's production changes. I then restored all four files.

This is a safety review because part alignment and WCS origin placement affect machining geometry. I ran two temporary mutations myself:

1. Restore `view_pose` in the cylinder axis reader: RED. The consecutive alignment test found the original axis at `[0.8386705679, 0, -0.5446390350]` instead of along Y.
2. Restore the active setup pose in the vertex origin reader: RED. The named setup test found `[30,50,50]` instead of `[35,35,60]`.

After restoration, all five MCP orientation tests passed again. No code edits remain.

Requested before merge: none for this PR.

No goldens moved. No UI files changed, so before/after screenshots are not required. No dependency, build.rs, scripts, or workflow changes were found. The current AGENTS.md requires the process declaration in the body and leaves PROCESS_VERSION to the merge batch; this PR follows that rule.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
